newsitem.title: UK: James Halstead slips on weaker H1 results.
newsitem.headline: James Halstead slips on weaker H1 results.

text.p: Shares in James Halstead Group Plc fell on Tuesday after the flooring, trailer, and outdoor clothing manufacturer's first-half results showed a drop in turnover, pre-tax profit and earnings per share.
The stock slipped 26p to 307-1/2 by 1110 GMT -- its lowest since the group's stock market flotation in March 1995.

First-half results for the half-year ending December 31 showed turnover dropping 1.3 percent to 37.6 million stg and a 15 percent fall in pre-tax profit to 4.2 million stg, while earnings per share slipped to 9.16p from 10.88p.
The company said the decline was due to disappointing performances at its Driza-Bone and Conway units, which both suffered from weak sales and margins.

Group chairman Vincent Clare said he believed the second half results would show a significant improvement given reasonable success in future plans and a modest improvement in sales and trading conditions.

"Although we do not perceive it necessary to make further disposals of non-core businesses at this stage, we shall be conducting a review during the coming months aimed at focusing more sharply on the opportunities which exist in our core floorcoverings business," Clare said.
